title: The Semester of the water tower
premise: Isandro Reyes, a seventeen-year-old coder who has spent seven years hiding behind an anonymous account that exposes corruption in his rust-belt town, finds his late grandmother's recipe box stuffed with coded directions—not for food, but for the money she laundered through the town's water fund, and proof of who stole it. As he deciphers her legacy, he realizes his anonymous posts have been circling the same conspiracy all along, and that staying invisible was never really an option. When his best friend Marisol discovers his secret identity days before prom, Isandro must choose between protecting their friendship and publishing the truth. He publishes, loses her trust, faces the men who killed his grandmother's partner, and finally testifies—learning that justice outside the law still demands he stand in the light.
about_author: Lior Okonkwo is a former municipal auditor turned novelist who grew up above a laundromat in a town much like Halloway Falls. Their fiction explores how ordinary people inherit other people's secrets—and what it costs to spend them.

chapters.title: The Account That Knows Too Much
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. We meet him at 3 a.m., posting as @hollowwater about a rigged city contract, then deleting his tracks with ritual precision. His carefulness is almost tender—he checks the locks twice, lies smoothly at dinner. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as safety; the reader feels how exhausting invisibility has become.

chapters.title: Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Clearing out Abuela Rosa's kitchen after the funeral, he finds her recipe box: index cards in her handwriting that aren't recipes—numbers, dates, initials, one card reading 'start with the water.' Emotional beat: grief interrupted by vertigo; the first crack in his carefully sealed world.

chapters.title: What Grandma Actually Cooked
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, with flashbacks to age ten. He deciphers the first cards: Rosa kept books for the Halloway Falls water fund and recorded every skimmed dollar. The dates align eerily with @hollowwater's own posts. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear—his grandmother was braver than he ever was.

chapters.title: Marisol Knows My Coffee Order
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Prom committee chaos, and Marisol noticing Isandro flinching whenever the water tower comes up in the news. She covers for him without knowing why. Emotional beat: warm, funny, establishing the friendship whose loss will later cost everything.

chapters.title: The Man from the Utility Board
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A polite stranger named Dale Pruitt visits, asking questions about Rosa's 'papers.' Isandro lies well—but Pruitt leaves a business card that says more than it says. Emotional beat: the hunter arrives; paranoia becomes rational.

chapters.title: Card Forty-One
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Card forty-one names Rosa's old partner, Tomás Vega, who drowned in the reservoir in 1998—an accident Isandro now suspects wasn't. The last card is addressed to him by name. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as both gift and debt; the dead are watching.

chapters.title: Two-Factor Authentication
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Using his coding skills, he cross-references the ledger against public records and builds a map of the theft—leading straight to Councilman Brandt and, uncomfortably, to Pruitt's firm. Emotional beat: competence as armor; for one night he feels powerful instead of afraid.

chapters.title: The Almost-Telling
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. At the diner, Isandro nearly tells her everything, then swerves. Marisol, hurt by seven years of small evasions, starts keeping a list of his contradictions. Emotional beat: the friendship strains under weight neither will name yet.

chapters.title: Someone Else Is Reading
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. His anonymous account receives a message: 'Your grandmother would be proud. Stop while you can.' Someone has connected @hollowwater to Rosa. Emotional beat: cold dread; the safe distance between screen and life collapses.

chapters.title: The Water Tower Climb
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Isandro and Marisol climb the water tower on a dare-turned-ritual, and from the top he almost shows her the recipe box. Instead he asks what she'd do if someone she loved lied to protect her. Emotional beat: tenderness on a ledge; dramatic irony tightening.

chapters.title: Pruitt Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Pruitt offers college money and silence—a clean transaction. Isandro records the meeting on his phone, hands shaking. Emotional beat: temptation rendered reasonable, which makes refusing it harder; the price of survival gets a dollar figure.

chapters.title: Rosa's Letters
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Hidden behind the box's false bottom, letters show Rosa spent her last years trying to go to the authorities and being warned off—one letter mentions Tomás's daughter, who left town and never came back. Emotional beat: grief deepens into resolve; cowardice, he sees, is inherited too unless refused.

chapters.title: Prom Dress Fitting, Interrogation Room Energy
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Light chapter: dress shopping, banter, Marisol's own family pressures. But she catches Isandro photographing documents and confronts him gently. He says 'soon.' Emotional beat: the calm before; readers ache knowing 'soon' is a lie.

chapters.title: Breach
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Someone breaks into Rosa's house—not stealing anything, just searching. Isandro realizes they know the box exists but not where he keeps it. He moves the cards inside a hollowed-out calculus textbook. Emotional beat: violation and improvisation; safety is now something he builds hourly.

chapters.title: The Upload
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Two days before prom, @hollowwater publishes everything: ledgers, recordings, Rosa's letters. Then he does the thing he swore he'd never do—he signs it with his real name. Emotional beat: terrifying liberation; seven years of held breath released in one click.

chapters.title: Marisol Finds Out First
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She reads the post before school and realizes her best friend is the account she's followed for years—and that he let her sit beside the secret for months. The confrontation is quiet and devastating. Emotional beat: betrayal felt as arithmetic; trust doesn't shatter, it drains.

chapters.title: Prom Without Me
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Isandro skips prom; Pruitt's people follow him home; Marisol dances with someone else and hates every minute. Brandt goes on local news calling the leak 'a grieving boy's fantasy.' Emotional beat: the cost arrives exactly as promised—the friendship priced, and payment collected.

chapters.title: Tomás's Daughter
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He tracks down Elena Vega, who confirms the drowning and gives him the missing ledger page Rosa mailed her in 1999. She warns him: testimony made her a target once too. Emotional beat: solidarity across generations; he stops being alone in this.

chapters.title: The Reservoir at Night
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Lured by a fake message, Isandro is cornered at the reservoir by Pruitt's fixer. He survives because he planned for this—recording everything, backup already scheduled to publish if he goes silent. Emotional beat: climax of nerve; cleverness as self-defense, fear transmuted into leverage.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Before a packed county hearing, Isandro presents the full record—Rosa's books, Elena's page, his recordings. Brandt resigns mid-session; Pruitt is indicted. Justice comes not from the law alone but from a dead woman's index cards and a boy who stopped hiding. Emotional beat: catharsis; the truth spoken aloud in daylight.

chapters.title: What You Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol reads Rosa's letter to Isandro—the one that says 'tell the truth even if it costs you the people you love'—and understands why he waited so long to tell her. She shows up at his door. Not forgiveness yet, but the beginning of it. Emotional beat: repair attempted honestly; love choosing to try again.

chapters.title: The Semester Ends
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Graduation. The water tower gets repainted with Rosa's initials. Isandro archives @hollowwater and starts a new account—with his face on it—covering the school board next. Final beat: inheritance accepted; survival redefined as living visibly, with Marisol beside him and the recipe box finally just recipes on top.
